records.c: Armakuni's X at $54 and the active opponent's X at $56. The corresponding Y bytes are at $55 and $57.
High byte of the current player action script. The script stops when its next absolute target has a zero high byte.
High byte of the opponent's current action cursor. Zero leaves the interpreter idle.
Dispatch selector for the opponent control routine at $6A48.
Saved value of the game tick at the beginning of an opponent wait. The difference is compared with $CC before attempting an approach.
Pointer consulted when the VIC interrupts during a tape read. The tape IRQ handler jumps through it after acknowledging the VIC.
Set the reader mode and destination, install the tape IRQ, program CIA timer A, and wait for status $90 to reach $FD or higher.
Check mode bits then poll the reader status. Once the load terminates, disarm the CIA interrupt and return the end address in X and Y.
Acknowledge a VIC interrupt inside the tape reader, then dispatch through the saved vector at $0311.
Jump used by the tape reader to install its RAM IRQ vector. The loader copies the two operand bytes to $FFFE.
Read and acknowledge the CIA interrupt, restart timer A and rotate the sampled input into the receive shift register according to its state.
Shift input until the sync value $0F appears, then set the byte receiver state.
On a full byte, update the running XOR, save registers, and dispatch according to the active phase.
Compare the new byte to $0F. Reset the sync hunt or install the next receive-state branch.
Restore Y, X and A after handling a complete received byte.
Recognise the header lead-in and $AA sync marker. Reset the header index and checksum before receiving header bytes.
Compare the received bytes to the requested name. Extract the file parameters after the name bytes.
Reject a nonzero running XOR for the header and initialise the destination in load mode.
Select the next page or partial page length, transfer the receive loop to the data handler and advance the reader status.
Bank out ROM and I/O around each write to RAM. Advance the destination pointer and decrement the byte count. Verify mode compares RAM instead.
Set the reader status to $FF and return its state to the sync scanner.
Continue when another full or partial page remains. Otherwise signal completion with status $FD.
This captured boot image contains $20 bytes from the end of the reader to the end of its RAM page.
Cold boot entry jumps to the memory setup at $5409.
Jump entry for restoring the video registers and colour RAM.
Jump entry for the loading picture at $5DF4.
Initialise the processor port direction and enable the ROM and I/O configuration for the cold start. Jump to the chapter entry at $BC60.
Save the processor port, copy colour RAM and configure the VIC, then restore the caller's banking.
Copy the staged colour bytes at $C400–$C7E7 to the 1,000 colour cells at $D800–$DBE7. The last indexed copy overlaps the preceding one by 24 bytes.
Set the eight working and pending sprite Y positions to zero, clear the 30 by 18 playfield cells, and initialise the corresponding staged colour cells to $10.
Save the current game tick, reset the transient room variables, fetch the room's $AEE0 entry and set the two shared VIC sprite colours for the current chapter.
Six values written to VIC register $D025, indexed by chapter letter minus A.
Six values written to VIC register $D026, indexed by chapter letter minus A.
Clear the VIC interrupt flags, read CIA 1 interrupt status and restore Y, X and A.
Preserve the interrupted A, X and Y and step the loading track via $BF10. Use the common IRQ register restore.
Save A, X, Y and the CPU port. Select I/O with both ROMs banked out, then dispatch according to bit 7 of $D019.
Increment the tick byte $1B when the IRQ takes the non-VIC path and $02B7 is clear.
Write the sampled VIC interrupt register back to $D019 to acknowledge the asserted flags.
Restore Y, X and A and return from the interrupt. The paths that come here have already restored the processor port.
If $B700 is zero, call $B000 with X=$28 and Y=$B7 so the loaded music driver starts at its $B728 track header.
Hardware NMI entry. Return immediately without changing registers.
Eight single-bit masks. The keyboard reader complements each mask before writing it to CIA 1 port A to select one keyboard row.
Compare the tick difference for slot X with the interval table. Update the slot when it is due. Otherwise remove one return address so the caller also returns early.
Ignore steering while the forfeit or depletion flag is pending. Otherwise split the joystick port's direction and fire bits.
Clear the fire latch, translate the joystick direction bits, and compare the requested heading with the current facing.
While the entry flag is on, suppress changes more than one direction step away from the starting facing.
Turn when the requested diagonal is neither the current facing nor its opposite. A backward diagonal can keep the current facing.
Choose the walking action family and mirror flag according to the saved facing.
When the direction table returns a negative value, mark the player stationary. If the selected weapon changed and the current script has stopped, start its changeover action.
Compare the fire button with its previous state. A new press from rest selects the crouch pose. A new press while moving continues to the direction check.
Test the stick heading. The current heading and adjacent headings select the standing or forward action. Wider turns first try to pick up an item.
Use the action number and facing to select an animation pointer and save its action family. Start the chosen script via the common entry.
Store the given action pointer, save its first flags, and clear the timer so its first record is read on the next update.
Require the same direction for four ticks unless the preceding action has already primed the timer. Choose the action family using that direction and the current weapon.
Route held-fire input through the forward handler when the boundary action number is from $10 to $13.
Map the four active-high stick direction bits to eight headings. $FF marks neutral or unsupported direction combinations.
Two little-endian script addresses per action number, selected by the facing group.
Add one of these offsets to half the player's facing to form the action family number at $6D.
Zero-terminated text for the transition message that says the quest continues.
Combine player X, Y and facing with the current item's pickup rectangle. Reject occupied slots. Most object IDs below 10 require the inventory flag at $03EE.
Y and the facing-adjusted X must fall within the half-open rectangle at $027B–$027E.
If slot 2 is unoccupied, allow item 2 and the IDs at or above 10 and leave the other objects in place.
Item codes $10, $12 and $13 set effect or action state instead of taking an inventory slot. Item 1 checks the selected item before pickup.
Hide the room's item sprite and update its inventory slot. Item codes $0E and $0F start with $85 and 3 respectively. Other ordinary slots increment.
Draw the collected item, show its status caption, and start a 150-tick display timer. Refresh the colours of the available weapons.
Read the current tick and compute elapsed time. Continue the player's active action or check the input for a new one.
If flag bit 3 is clear, look for new input while a pose script is active, then continue with either the old or the new script.
Compute and commit collision-checked walking. Advance the walking frame when four ticks have accumulated or a redraw is pending.
Select the mirror input and walking pose from the saved movement and facing values, then publish the sprite group with the foreground mask.
Seed the movement test with the player's position, fractional offsets and the opponent coordinates. Store the accepted result back in the player state.
Run the same movement check with the actors swapped. If the new opponent coordinates are outside the playfield, clear its active type and pose state.
Subtract the last opponent update time from the game tick. Pass the elapsed ticks to the action interpreter with X equal to two.
Enter the action interpreter with X equal to zero for Armakuni.
If a script is active, subtract the elapsed ticks from the current pose's timer. Decode the next record on expiry. Flag bit 2 requests a hit test while the timer is still running.
Read a record's flags. Bit 1 supplies a new tick duration. Always read the pose index and reuse the previous duration if the optional duration byte is absent.
When flag bit 7 is set, add the record's signed X and Y offsets. The opponent branch handles crossing the positive X limit separately.
Bit 0 introduces an effect byte. Effects $10–$1F consume another byte whose low bits and next three bits initialise $D3 and $D4.
Bit 5 replaces the action cursor with the following little-endian address. Otherwise skip the bytes consumed by this record.
Run the player or opponent contact test according to the actor index and restore the index before returning to the pose interpreter.
Choose the player or opponent pose components, then pass the actor's depth to the foreground mask routine before publishing its sprites.

Choose picture slot 1, set up the bitmap display, clear its playfield, and fall through to the chapter picture renderer.
Index the five-byte record at $0808 + 5 times the picture slot in $A2. Apply its background colour, then look up its shape script through one of the two pointer pages.
Resolve the current selector through one of two pointer pages. An untagged pointer calls a nested script and saves the parent script cursor on the stack.
Clear the descriptor tag, split width and height into nibbles, and read the placement X and Y from the current script record.
Use bits 5–6 of the placement's Y byte as a count of remaps. Each extra byte maps its low-nibble colour to its high-nibble colour.
Calculate bitmap and screen addresses for the placement from its row lookups and X offset. Also point to the two source colour arrays after the bitmap bytes.
Read both colours for this cell, apply the remaps, and copy the colour and bitmap data or pass the cell to the overlap routine.
Advance to the next eight-byte cell unless the row reaches the shape width or the 30-cell playfield boundary.
Advance the source colours and destination screen pointers. Advance the bitmap to the next row and skip any clipped source columns.
Bit 6 of the X byte ends this level of the script. Return to the parent script if present, otherwise end the draw.
Skip the four base bytes and the extra colour remaps, then resolve the next placement.
Low bytes for the 18 playfield bitmap rows, 320 bytes apart from $E000.
Matching high bytes of the bitmap row starts used for shape placement.
Low bytes of the 18 screen colour rows, 40 bytes apart from $C000.
Matching high bytes for the playfield screen colour rows.
Read the used palette slots from the destination auxiliary colour flags. Compare the new cell's colours to the background and those already in the cell before adding its pixels.
When the source flags say this colour is present, match its high screen nibble to an existing slot or allocate a free one.
Map the source screen byte's low nibble in the same way when the corresponding source flag is set.
Map the source auxiliary colour to a destination palette slot when used. If a required colour has no slot, try to free a slot before rematching the colours.
Write the two screen colour nibbles and the auxiliary nibble and palette usage flags. Prepare to combine the raster bytes.
Map each nonzero source bit pair to its destination palette code. Preserve the original pair for transparent or unavailable colours, and repeat for eight raster rows.
The four destination pixel codes positioned in bits 0–1 of a bitmap byte.
Destination pixel codes shifted into bits 2–3.
Destination pixel codes shifted into bits 4–5.
Destination pixel codes shifted into bits 6–7.
Count destination colour codes in pixels where the source is transparent. Reclaim unused slots, and if more slots are needed prefer the least-used unreserved colour.
For each unused destination colour, clear its usage flag. Count the slots available to assign to the incoming shape.
If the available slots are insufficient, discard the least frequent colour that is eligible for replacement and repeat the count.
Select a panel area from X and clear its two rows of colour cells. A equal to 10 hides the current icon, 0 to 9 draws an inventory item, and higher values select a weapon picture.
Compute a 64-byte item bitmap address at $DC80 plus 64 times the item number. Copy its eight colour cells and its two bitmap rows into the selected panel.
Expose RAM beneath I/O and copy 32 bytes into each destination row. Restore the CPU port after the two rows.
Use the selected weapon descriptor to find the panel offset, bitmap, width, height, and its two colour arrays. Copy bands of cells a row at a time.
Five offsets selecting 12-byte weapon picture descriptors for item codes 11 through 15.
Two little-endian bitmap addresses used for the Using and Holding panels.
Two little-endian screen matrix addresses for those same panels.
Five 12-byte records, one per weapon picture. Each gives bitmap and screen bases, width and height, placement offset, and two colour array addresses.
Walk the weapon picture descriptors and the five inventory slots at $03F7. Copy a weapon's palette data when owned or zero its display colours when unavailable.
Advance the three screen destinations one 40-byte row and the two source arrays by the width of the weapon picture.
When the message timer at $A0 expires, redraw the selected weapon and its status icon.
After the current player pose ends, handle the depletion or forfeit request at $B6 by choosing the falling action cursor.
Character codes for the embedded sentence that credits John Twiddy with the programming.
Wait for the first raster line. Select multicolour bitmap mode, the VIC bank and the bitmap address, and load the two shape-pointer page bases from $0800–$0801.
Set the VIC raster compare to line 8, reload CIA 1 timer A from $028C–$028D, and install the game's RAM IRQ vectors before enabling interrupts.
Wait for the CIA-driven counter at $1B to change A times. X counts down between changes.
Walk the $CC00 stream to the section for the picture slot in $A2, skipping groups delimited by $EE when the slot is between 2 and 27.
Read a starting X and Y followed by pairs of control and length. Expand each pair into X0, Y0, X1, Y1 and flags at $0334.
A chain starts at the current stream cursor unless the next byte is $EE. End the decoded list with a zero X and Y in that case.
Subtract the even part of the length from X for a segment drawn leftwards, compute its Y displacement and store the smaller X endpoint first. Flip the slope sign for the reordered endpoints.
Multiply X by Y with an eight-bit shift-and-add loop. Return the low byte in X and the high byte in Y.
Compare the movement endpoints in $48–$4B to the decoded collision segments. Evaluate the segment slope at both X coordinates to detect a change of side.
Copy the middle 64-byte image at $DB40 from under I/O and place it in the weapon status region.
Select the last 64-byte image at $DB80 in the status bitmap copy.
Select the first 64-byte image at $DB00 and enter the status bitmap copy.
Copy one 64-byte bitmap from RAM under the I/O registers. Set its eight screen bytes, staged colour bytes and VIC colour RAM cells.
Three rows of eight screen colour combinations, one row for each corresponding source at $DB00, $DB40 or $DB80.
Three rows of eight colour RAM values for the three small status images drawn at $EAF8.
When the high bit of $CB is set and timer slot 12 is due, dispatch the opponent behaviour through its current state at $CF.
Fold the facing direction at $6B into the supplied base action number and save the result at $6F.
Check the opponent flags and a random byte before assigning one of two waiting states. The AND with immediate zero prevents the branch directly to the sideways movement.
Choose a two-step turn to either side from a random bit. Save the start X, dispatch action $18 and set the action number for that facing.
If the opponent has moved at least 32 pixels in the selected X direction, flip its horizontal facing and reissue the side movement action.
Choose a random delay, adding 16 ticks when $72 is nonzero. Save the current tick and set opponent state 3.
Continue the sideways state or wait for the countdown. When the wait expires, start the sideways or approach action.
Set state 5, face the player and call the chapter action entry with X equal to eight.
Choose a point to approach offset from the player according to the player's facing, then measure the distance from the opponent to that point.
Save the player's position, face it, dispatch chapter action four, and set state 6 for the close-range decision.
For opponent type $88, bring its X back within 4 to 247 before starting the close-range action.
If player X has moved by at least $B0 from its saved value and the actors are far apart, try the type $80 or $81 special action. Otherwise steer the approach.
Compare the direction to the player with the direction to the target point. Rate-limit horizontal reversals and restart the walking action on a facing change.
Wait after the current damage action. Otherwise choose one of the close actions using a random value and the active $72 variant.
Once in state 8, compare player X and Y with the saved close-range position. Time another decision if the player stays nearby, or restart the approach after movement.
When state 9 is active, wait for both the current opponent pose and its extra actor to finish before starting another approach.
Horizontal spacing values selected by the active opponent variant at $72.
Map the eight direction values to the facing adjustment used by the approach decision.
Two little-endian action script addresses chosen by bit 2 of the opponent's facing.
Measure both absolute coordinate differences and add them, saturating the result at $FF.
Measure the distance from the X coordinate in A, with the player's Y unchanged.
Subtract the requested amount from the power byte at $C8. On reaching zero, choose the depletion pose and set $B6.
Accumulate the active opponent's wounds up to $20, save the result in the room's $AEE0 slot and redraw the bars.
Combine horizontal and vertical comparisons of the actors' coordinates, then translate the quadrant to a facing value.
Use an explicit X target in A for the horizontal comparison while keeping the player Y target.
Directions 7, 5, 1 and 3 corresponding to the four coordinate comparison outcomes.
Reset common transient state, including the extra actor state and pending exit and retry flags.
Clear room wounds and reset power to $20. Copy the saved 20-byte inventory into the active slots and restore the stored life count and status icons.
Convert a held apple to a life, save the life count and inventory, and carry at least two lives out of the Wastelands when one was left.
Clear the script active bytes of both main actors and the current and pending Y coordinates of all eight hardware sprites.
Read port 2 into $B5 with the joystick bits active high. Scan eight keyboard rows into $0260–$0267 when port B is idle, then check changes in the keys.
Fill the eight key rows with $FF when bits on CIA port B are active. Skip directly to the checks that use the row variables.
Drive a complemented single-bit row mask on CIA port A, read CIA port B, and save each row as active-low bits.
Process the F1 press edge via latch $02AA. Invert the enable byte $AA, and when it becomes zero clear $D400–$D417.
On an F3 press, find the next occupied entry in the 11-slot item inventory at $03EC and update the Holding display.
On an F5 press, decrement the held item index with wraparound and skip slots that contain zero. Update its icon in the status panel.
Use the saved F7 key bit to identify a press edge, then invert $02B7. The tick IRQ checks this byte before incrementing $1B.
On a Space press, when $0280 is clear, step forward through six weapon slots at $03F6 and skip those whose low seven bits are zero.
Check either Shift key, then inspect the minus and plus key bits. Pass the updated timer word at $028C–$028D to CIA 1 timer A.
Holding minus with Shift increases the timer period one high byte at each key scan, up to $80.
Holding plus with Shift decreases the timer period one high byte at each key scan while its high byte is at least $20.
When Run/Stop is held, set $B6 to $FF. While the pause byte is set, stay in the control scan instead of returning to the game loop.
Sixteen values map each VIC colour to the next shade during the display fade.
Expose the under-I/O RAM and look up the room at $DF00. For each eligible component, apply its foreground shapes when the depth at $84 is no greater than their cutoffs.
Protect the pending sprite coordinates, bitmap pointers and flags from the raster interrupt while updating them. Flip the working bitmap bank after publishing a changed component.
Publish changed sprite positions, flags and bitmap bank pointers in one interrupt-protected pass.
Convert the stored cell to VIC pixel coordinates by multiplying by eight and adding the playfield offsets $18 and $32. Unpack the shape selector for the mask reader.
Select the low 15 bits of the pointer and expand both cell dimensions into pixel counts.
Test the top, bottom, left and right limits of the foreground shape against the sprite. Save pixel offsets within the overlapping portion.
Mark this sprite as masked, then calculate the width and height of the overlap clipped to both the sprite and the foreground shape.
Select this sprite's working bank and compute where the overlap starts in both the sprite RAM and the source shape.
A nonzero pair of bits in the foreground bitmap clears the corresponding two bits from the sprite. Advance to the next affected sprite position.
Move down one raster line. Repeat a row of the sprite source for expanded height and advance eight-row cell blocks in the foreground bitmap.
Map a horizontal position from 0 to 23 to its byte in a three-byte sprite row.
Masks that clear one adjacent pair of sprite bits and preserve the other six.
Masks that clear a single sprite bit and preserve the other seven.
A nonzero source pixel clears one bit in the sprite at the overlapping position. Select the sprite mask by its horizontal pixel offset.
Eight masks of the form $FF shifted left by 0 through 7 bits. The final zero is also in the lookup.
Little-endian addresses at 40-byte strides for all 25 rows of the screen matrix at $C000.
Little-endian addresses at 320-byte strides for all 25 rows of the VIC bitmap at $E000.
Repeatedly choose a random byte and bit pair in the first 256 bytes of both sprite banks. Clear those bits in both banks, then zero the affected banks completely.
Test the candidate coordinates in $54–$55. Once they pass the playfield boundary, map the point to a clockwise value and index the eight-byte room row at $AF00.
Compare the edge coordinate to four ascending thresholds. Use the first greater threshold or wrap to the first entry.
Read the selected destination byte from the second half of the eight-byte edge row and save it at $0278.
Shift the destination right twice to find the next room. A zero room sets $02AF to request the tape transition.
Use the full destination byte to index the variant table at $FF3C. Copy the resulting spawn coordinates and facing from $FFB8, $FFD8 and $AFE0.
Fractional X step values. Position zero is for Armakuni and the remaining positions are for the opponent's movement variants.
Fractional Y step values for the same actor classes.
Whole X step values paired with the fractional X increments.
Whole Y step values paired with the fractional Y increments.
Repeat the requested movement for each elapsed tick. Direction masks select signed fixed-point X and Y increments. Commit each step only when it passes the room and opponent checks.
Subtract the chosen X step and clamp to zero if it goes below the left limit.
Add the X step and clamp to $FE on overflow.
When the heading calls for northward movement, subtract the Y increment. Double the increment where the direction mask allows it.
Mirror the northward test for southward movement, adding the regular or doubled increment.
Check the compressed room boundaries for the player. For either actor, if the opponent type is active, reject motion within 12 horizontal pixels and the current vertical spacing.
Save the candidate coordinates and continue until the elapsed ticks are used.
Record the collision class, restore the last accepted whole-pixel coordinates and return $FF.
Four masks that indicate leftward travel for each facing group.
Four masks that indicate rightward travel for each facing group.
Direction bits that enable movement towards the top of the bitmap.
Direction bits that enable movement towards the bottom of the bitmap.
Directions that apply the Y step twice.
Directions that suppress the Y update.
Heading masks that select whether the player advances the walk pose in its regular or reverse order.
Masks that pick or clear the mirror flag according to the player's facing group.
Select the opponent variant and its mirroring flag, then enter the shared sprite component reader.
Clear the actor redraw request and use the current weapon to select the player component class.
Bank out I/O. Use 32-byte descriptors below index $40, shorter descriptors from $40, and chapter descriptors from $80 upward.
Multiply the selected pose ID by 32, form its pointer under I/O at $D000, and use its mirror origin and component records.
Clear the four component Y positions, fill the available components, and optionally apply an opponent variant or an extra actor.
Use the activity and variant bytes to choose a packed sprite, palette, and position offsets. Copy its bitmap into the working bank.
If the opponent is active and its type is below $84, use the selected $D4 palette entry for sprite component 4.
Sprite IDs indexed by the toggling phase of the extra actor.
Matching colour values for the alternate extra actor states.
Small X offsets used to place the extra actor sprite.
Small Y offsets paired with the X offsets selected by the low two state bits.
Signed X and Y offsets read when a weapon or special effect launches an extra actor. Its facing selects the first offset.
Eight bitmap indices for the cycling extra actor pose.
Eight matching VIC colour values for the cycling pose.
Skip a component with ID $FF. Otherwise call the component builder. Mark the selected hardware sprite for publication and move to the following descriptor.
Clear working and pending Y positions for sprites 4–7. Stop the opponent action script.
Zero-terminated first line of the closing message.
A random byte of at least $40 clears the opponent sprites and returns $FF. Otherwise leave the opponent active and return zero.
Fetch zero-terminated character codes via $02. Use X and Y as the starting cell, and A to fill the staged colour for each two-by-two-cell glyph.
Multiply the character code by eight and form the glyph address from $D800. Calculate the bitmap and staged colour addresses for its placement.
Switch the CPU port to expose character ROM, then double each glyph pixel in both directions into the bitmap.
Restore the caller's banking, move across two cells and pick up the next character code.
Mix the low CIA timer byte and a byte from the sampled engine code range $5400–$7EFF into the random value. Move the code cursor on for the next call.
Fetch the bitmap address for the selected hardware sprite. If working-bank bit 0 is set, advance the address by $200.
Copy each three-byte row from $02C0 into the selected working buffer. Apply the per-column clipping masks.
Reverse each byte's bits through $9D00 and reverse their order within each row before applying the clipping masks.
Eight auxiliary colour cells for each of the ten inventory images. The status painter uses four per row.
Eight screen colour pairs for each inventory icon in the same order as the auxiliary palette.
Update eight bitmap blocks from the wound count saved at $02B9. Use the fractional bar patterns for partially filled blocks.
Four byte patterns forming the partial-cell widths of the opponent wounds bar.
A pose byte of $FF hides four sprites. Other negative values choose a 16-byte chapter descriptor at $D800 plus 16 times the low seven bits.
Read the shorter pose entries. Skip or hide $FF components according to the accompanying flags and build the visible ones.
Fade $28 columns and 25 rows of screen colours with the palette mapping at $6FE1. Also fade the background, active sprite colours and VIC shared sprite colours.
Use the same fade for 30 columns and 18 rows of the screen.
Wait at the game tick and raster boundaries, then remap the background and sprite colours and each cell of the requested rectangle.
Choose random playfield bytes, then clear one multicolour pixel position in two adjacent bitmap rows. Repeat for this batch of selections.
